observed_problem: The compact agent-first Stage Checkpoint bound supplied artifact hashes, but several lifecycle stages had no configured canonical artifacts. Screening, Evidence/Materiality/Completeness, Selection, Draft/Synthesis and Validation could therefore theoretically advance with a PASS review row while binding no authoritative stage output bytes.
expected_behavior: Every local lifecycle transition must bind the existing canonical logical artifacts that establish that stage's authority. Compact checkpoints may remove request/receipt ceremony, but they must not permit review-only advancement without exact artifact provenance.
actual_behavior: The Stage Checkpoint schema is now lifecycle-aware and requires the canonical logical artifact set for every transition: discovery acceptance; screening acceptance; evidence/views/materiality/completeness authorities; candidate matrix/selection; Architecture review package; synthesis input/result; validated source/PDF/quality bundle; Publication Candidate; Freeze authorities; and Release verification/record. Each named artifact remains SHA-bound in the checkpoint.
improvement_action: Implemented by requiring lifecycle-specific existing canonical artifact authorities directly in the compact Stage Checkpoint schema and adding a regression that rejects review-only Screening advancement.
